verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents adding experiment rules to feature flags that randomly assign users to variations. Results are computed against warehouse-defined metrics, and a Chance to Win readout highlights a clear winner in green. Community users report getting flags and A/B tests running in hours. missing for 10: explicit documentation of multivariate (3+ arm) experiments beyond the generic 'variations' wording, and hands-on or independent corroboration of the results and winner-picking view.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can run A/B and multivariate experiments on flags and see which variation wins on my metrics

citations.quote: you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.
Chance to Win tells you the probability that the variation is better. Anything above 95% ... is highlighted green indicating a very clear winner.
see the impact of your experiment on your metrics.
The primary way to create metrics in GrowthBook is with Fact Tables where you write SQL to pull a set of rows and then define multiple metrics on top of those rows.
we got FF and A/B in our Vue frontend in a few hours.
